title: Change Todo software and contracts
summary: Modify Todo code, CLI, database, research stages, decisions, email, installation, or public behavior.
use_when: Todo code, tests, public CLI, database, liaisons, authorization, email, installation, or release behavior is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary use or operation of installed Todo.
The change belongs to Nucleus shared execution rather than Todo domain behavior.
Release publication or deployment has not been separately authorized.
outcome: A minimal tested Todo change that preserves durable provenance and the separation between research proposals, explicit decisions, desired design, and implementation execution.
effects: Modifies Todo source, tests, migrations, documentation, or packaging.
May change requester toolsets, prompts, state schema, email disclosure, or installed service behavior with corresponding compatibility and recovery obligations.
Release and deployment remain separate actions with Git, database, service, email, and external-state effects.
authority: Todo owns concerns, routing, decisions, identities, directions, assessments, designs, lifecycle, notes, email projection, database, and installation.
Nucleus owns execution and authentication but cannot authorize Todo decisions or implementation.
success: All changed public and operational contracts are documented and immutable historical records remain meaningful.
Affected Nucleus requester, database migration, email, and deployment canaries are run when their boundaries change.
failure_and_recovery: Preserve a committed Todo domain result when a later Nucleus error occurs.
Version immutable Nucleus schemas and toolsets rather than editing historical registrations.
Use backup-bearing migrations and deployment rollback rather than ad hoc database repair.
privacy: Todo fixtures, databases, backups, decision sources, Nucleus output, email content, API configuration, and logs may contain private directions and system state.
Model stages receive only frozen bounded sources through managed tools and must not gain shell, workspace, or web access accidentally.
steps: Identify the Todo-owned layer being changed and preserve the distinctions among `cN`, `rN`, `tN`, `aN`, `dN`, notes, lifecycle, and external implementation.
Run `nucleus manual` before changing requester tools, shared execution, authentication, compatibility, job records, persistent cross-system state, or deployment.
Implement the smallest change and update CLI, liaison, architecture, data, or installation documentation in the same change.
Run `./todo/ci.sh` and perform separately authorized live canaries when required.
checkpoints: Model text remains non-authoritative and explicit accept/reject commands remain outside liaison tools.
Todo does not become an implementation workflow, project graph, or evidence that work ran.
Persistent changes have migration, backup, rollback, and historical compatibility proof.
Release or deployment has not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Select the exact domain documentation for the changed layer and use the current installed Nucleus manual for shared runtime facts.
Scale live canaries to the effects: routing, assessment, design, email, migration, and installation exercise different authorities.
stop_when: A proposed shortcut would let a model accept a decision or treat execution as Todo state.
A destructive migration or external email change lacks explicit authority and recovery.
The shared Nucleus boundary is changing without the corresponding owning contract work.
does_not_authorize: Running `todo/release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying Todo or migrating the installed database.
Sending email or changing external Resend state.

consumers.statement: An interactive developer authorized to change the Todo repository may use this operation for Todo-owned code, tests, contracts, documentation, migrations, packaging, or release workflow.
Ordinary Todo use, independent Nucleus changes, release publication, deployment, database migration, and email sending are not implied by this development operation.

preconditions.statement: The developer has the Todo source, applicable Semantics and installed contract context, and authority to modify the requested Todo-owned boundary.
Requester, persistent-state, compatibility, service, deployment, or integration changes first consult the current Nucleus manual and identify coordinated owner obligations.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the requested Todo change, current product source and tests, exact owning domain and operational documentation, installed contracts, and any authorized compatibility or recovery constraints.
Model prose, historical notes, or a Nucleus terminal job cannot replace current Todo source, tests, explicit decisions, or separately authorized external effects.

outputs.statement: The output is the smallest coherent Todo source and documentation change with affected tests, migration or rollback proof, and product CI results proportional to the boundary changed.
This operation does not itself output a published release, deployed installation, migrated user database, sent email, or implemented underlying tN direction.

data_semantics.statement: Changes preserve the distinctions among immutable cN concern, rN proposal and decision, enduring tN umbrella, dated aN observation, normative dN design, immutable nN note, lifecycle, and external implementation.
Nucleus jobs are research provenance and execution state, not Todo decision authority or evidence that an accepted design was implemented.

identity_and_units.statement: Todo package and provider release, entry contract version, SQLite schema version, Nucleus toolset and result-schema versions, and public domain IDs evolve as distinct identities.
The development operation publishes no implementation-effort, schedule, cost, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Completion requires every affected code, test, CLI, liaison, architecture, data, installation, and authored-contract surface to agree and the Todo product CI gate to pass.
Current installed manuals and source documentation are reread for the selected boundary; separately authorized live canaries are required only when their actual runtime boundary changed.
Passing source tests alone does not establish a released, deployed, migrated, emailed, or externally successful outcome.

access.statement: The operation uses only the interactive developer's authorized local filesystem and shell surfaces for scoped Todo repository work and validation.
It grants no production database, Nucleus credential, Resend account, recipient, release publication, or installed-state authority.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Immutable historical records, schemas, and toolsets remain meaningful; incompatible changes publish new versions and persistent changes include transactional migration, backup, and rollback.
A Todo domain commit can outlive a later Nucleus error and must remain recoverable rather than being rolled back or duplicated from runtime state.

operational_limits.statement: The operation is limited to the smallest Todo-owned change and its proportional tests and documentation; it stops at another owner's unresolved boundary or unauthorized external effect.
No development duration, review turnaround, release cadence, or deployment schedule is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 requires immutable Nucleus registration identities, meaningful historical Todo records, and synchronized public and operational documentation for incompatible changes.
Release publication and deployment remain separately authorized operations even when development changes their source workflows.
No universal support window or deprecation period for Todo releases, schemas, or integrations is promised.

reliances.statement: Todo development relies on its registered Semantics repository for maintained project terminology while source, tests, and product documentation remain authoritative for behavior.
This terminology authority does not create a Todo runtime reliance; any other cross-system boundary is governed and validated through its separately selected owning contract.
